constraints.text: Two roads diverged in a wood, and I— / I took the one less traveled by, / And that has made all the difference. (epigraph)
constraints.reading: The hiding spot may be at or just off a fork/junction where a path splits, and reached by the lesser/fainter of two trails — the less-trodden branch, not the main one.

constraints.text: Two roads diverged in a wood
constraints.reading: The spot is set within woods/forest cover, near a trail divergence — look for a Y-split or side spur.

constraints.text: digging for quartz crystals in a 'red dirt embankment'
constraints.reading: Reddish soil / red-clay embankment as a ground/color marker; the spot may be at or beside a sloped earthen bank of red dirt.

constraints.text: walking down the sloped street ... to a cul-de-sac, taking a sharp left ... onto a dog-worn path that followed a metal chain-link fence and ended at an empty lot
constraints.reading: A movement template: descend a slope, reach a dead-end/turnaround, turn sharply left, follow a faint path along a linear boundary (fence line) to its end. Spot is at the terminus of a path that hugs a fence or edge.

constraints.text: a dog-worn path ... ended at an empty lot — his 'excavation site'
constraints.reading: Destination is the END of a worn, informal footpath at an open/empty clearing.

constraints.text: hoping each unearthed rock would be clear or rose quartz rather than dark smoky quartz
constraints.reading: Pale/clear or rosy-pink quartz stone as a possible visual marker at the spot; contrast against darker rock.

constraints.text: studying striations in 300-million-year-old sandstone
constraints.reading: Layered/striated sandstone outcrop as a possible rock-type marker; look for visible bedding lines in stone.

constraints.text: another precocious boy ... was digging in a worn hillside
constraints.reading: A weathered/worn hillside as the type of feature; spot may be on the eroded face of a hill.

constraints.text: the mine sat near 'a very particular outlook,' the only vista where the Andes range opened up and 'the Plains of the Llanos could be seen below'
constraints.reading: CENTRAL spatial clue: the spot is at/near a distinctive OVERLOOK — a unique vantage point that is the ONE place a long view opens up over lower flat land below. Look for an overlook where distant lowlands are visible.

constraints.text: 'a view gaped open between two jagged grey peaks,' framing the green rolling Plains ... below
constraints.reading: The sightline is FRAMED between two jagged grey rock peaks/pinnacles — a gap or notch between two stones/crags through which lower land is seen. The framing pair of grey rocks is itself the locator.

constraints.text: two jagged grey peaks
constraints.reading: Paired pointed/jagged grey rock formations; the spot is the saddle/gap/notch between two such grey crags.

constraints.text: the green rolling Plains of the Llanos below
constraints.reading: The spot is HIGH/elevated, looking DOWN onto comparatively flat or rolling low ground; there is a marked elevation difference between the vantage and what is viewed.

constraints.text: the mine sat ... on a high ridge overlooking the River Rucio (research, Restrepo account)
constraints.reading: The vantage overlooks flowing water — a river/stream visible below the high point. Spot is on a ridge above a watercourse.

constraints.text: the only place where Los Llanos ... were visible through a V-notch in the range to the east (research)
constraints.reading: The opening/notch and the distant view face EAST; the framed sightline points toward the eastern lowlands. Orientation of the view is eastward.

constraints.text: a specific, repeatable sightline (a notch/gap framing a distant view) is what pinpoints the spot (research synthesis)
constraints.reading: Confirmation criterion: stand at the spot and a specific framed view should line up. The hiding place is identified by a precise sightline through a gap, not by terrain alone.

constraints.text: Restrepo found the ridge ... and uncovered old terraces and aqueduct remains (research)
constraints.reading: Once at the vantage, nearby man-made stone features (terraces, channels, walls) marked the exact spot — look for old stonework / built remnants near the overlook.

constraints.text: he hiked the Andes on 'well-worn trail ways' and 'there is no jungle clearing required ... your task is a much, much easier one'
constraints.reading: Spot is reachable on an established, well-worn trail — not bushwhacking. Accessible footpath leads to it; consistent with near-a-road, not-dangerous constraints.

constraints.text: emeralds don't sparkle. They shine ... green is the color most visible to the human eye
constraints.reading: Green may be a salient color cue at the spot (green vista, green stone, mossy/green feature) — the thing to spot is green and visible rather than glittering.

constraints.text: the abandoned mine was overgrown by Andes forest ... and lay hidden for 200 years; likened to 'the jungle surrounding the Angkor temples'
constraints.reading: The spot may be in or near a partly overgrown / hidden feature — concealed by vegetation, not in the open; possibly near an old structure reclaimed by growth.

constraints.text: Pilot Mountain ... capped by TWO bare-rock pinnacles ... connected by a narrow saddle (research analogue)
constraints.reading: Generic landform echo of the chapter motif: two bare rock summits joined by a saddle, with an overlook framing distant low country. The spot may sit at such a saddle/gap between twin rock outcrops.

constraints.text: a notable gap between Cooks Wall and Devils Chimney (Hanging Rock analogue, research)
constraints.reading: Reinforces a 'gap between two named rock features' geometry as the spatial signature to look for.

constraints.text: Window Rock / the Windows ... frame distant landscape through rock (research analogue)
constraints.reading: Alternate reading of the 'view gaped open' image: a natural rock window/arch/hole through which a distant view is framed — the spot may be at a window-rock opening.
